last_report.golden_diff_summary:
Ran diff_labels with --variants A on RunT1, RunT1T2E, RunT1T2RT2E, RunT2E, RunT2E[rotation], RunInterleavedCoherence and RunAutoCoherence[fast]. Also ran --variants B on RunT1 and RunT2E. Every captured T1FF and T2EMUX instantiation changes the same way:
- One 'methods.call' leaf: the display entry gains a new 'sets' {fit: {...}}. The classifier files a whole new 'sets' key under methods.call.
- Eight 'data_digest' leaves: new datasets <prefix>_fit_{a,c,err_us,ok,perr,popt,rotation_rad,us} on save_data.

Counts per label:
- RunT1: 4 T1FF, giving 4 + 32 leaves.
- RunT2E and RunT2E[rotation]: 4 T2EMUX each, 4 + 32. Under [rotation], t2e_fit_rotation_rad = 0.3, the cfg value.
- RunT1T2E and RunT1T2RT2E: 4 T1FF + 4 T2EMUX, 8 + 64. T2R is unchanged.
- RunInterleavedCoherence: 4 T1FF, 4 + 32. No T2EMUX is captured inside the budget, so T2E is not exercised in this label.
- RunAutoCoherence[fast]: 3 T1FF + 3 T2EMUX, 6 + 48.
- B: RunT1 and RunT2E show the same 4 + 32 pattern.

All 36 captured fits on the synthetic two-blob noise are ok False, as intended for noise. There are no cfg, hw/program-hash, cfg_digest/cfg_delta or cfg_access diffs, and no outcome changes.

Every label also shows 4-6 'yoko_writes' leaves (an extra OUTP?/FUNC?/RANG? query sequence). These are not from this change: RunT2 (T2R only, which this change does not touch) shows the identical yoko_writes diff and nothing else. They come from the concurrent uncommitted qicklab/hardware/yoko.py change by another agent. The orchestrator must attribute them to that commit, not this one.

last_report.notes:
Design choices the orchestrator should know:
(1) fit_exp_decay now returns a dict instead of the old tuple (T1_fit, T1_est, T1_err). The only consumers were T1FF.display and T2EMUX.display, so no compatibility shim was kept. T is no longer passed through abs(): the bounds keep it positive.
(2) I added a criterion the spec did not ask for: |a| >= 3 a_err. With only the spec's checks (bound hit, finite covariance, T_err < T), 6% of pure-noise traces gave ok True, so the "noise gives ok False" requirement would not hold reliably. With the check the rate is 0.3%. On a genuine but marginal decay (SNR about 1 per point) it rejects some fits that would otherwise pass. The constant is EXP_DECAY_MIN_A_SIGMAS in fitting.py.
(3) Added a small helper exp_decay_fit_fields(fit, prefix) in fitting.py, next to fit_exp_decay, that flattens the result into the h5 keys. Both displays share it.
(4) t1_fit_ok is stored as a Python bool. Its digest dtype is 'bool' and the h5 holds 1.0/0.0 because H5File.add forces float64.
(5) Nothing in tProc programs changed, so tests/test_program_timing.py is unchanged with no pin changes. Checks: compileall is clean, ruff F passes, ruff format was applied to the 4 touched .py files, and tests/test_exp_decay_fit.py, test_finish.py, test_imports.py, test_program_timing.py and test_ramsey_fit.py all pass.
(6) No git index or tree operations were performed. The golden, the fixtures, driver_legacy.py and symbol_map.py were not touched.
